claims.text: The tested material is an as-cast, thermally stabilized, multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The constituent phases are initially covered by continuous protective oxide or passive films.
Mechanical wear ruptures the protective oxide or passive layer.
Oxide-film rupture occurs preferentially at phase boundaries.
Rupture of the surface oxide film promotes adhesive and abrasive wear.
Compositional differences between constituent phases produce electrochemical potential differences.
Potential differences between dissimilar phases create localized galvanic cells.
The interphase potential difference facilitates electron transfer at phase boundaries and accelerates selective dissolution.
Wear-induced film rupture exposes the dissimilar phases and thereby activates localized galvanic corrosion.
Localized corrosion can dissolve or break down the protective film and expose the underlying alloy.
Corrosion-induced film degradation exacerbates mechanical wear.
Mutual reinforcement between corrosion and wear establishes a positive feedback loop that accelerates total degradation.
Under simultaneous wear and corrosion, total degradation will be significantly greater than the sum of degradation measured in separate wear-only and corrosion-only tests.
Simultaneous exposure will increase localized corrosion at phase boundaries relative to the isolated-exposure baselines.
Simultaneous exposure will increase the wear rate because oxide protection is lost.
The proposed coupled mechanism applies at elevated temperature in a chloride-rich medium under mechanical loading.
The proposed acceleration operates only when wear and corrosion act concurrently to disrupt the oxide layer at phase boundaries.
The magnitude of synergistic degradation depends on the extent of film disruption and the potential difference between phases.

contradictions.description: The baseline calls for a wear-only test under identical environmental conditions, but retaining the aggressive chloride environment would make that test a simultaneous wear-corrosion exposure. The experimental design instead describes a 'pure mechanical wear' condition without clarifying whether the corrosive medium is absent or electrochemically suppressed.
